edge_cases: Missing form fields cause a server error (e.g., KeyError) because the code accesses them directly.
Adding a book with a title that already exists results in a redirect back to the add page without insertion.
Login with incorrect credentials returns "Invalid credentials" even if the username exists.
Updating or deleting a non‑existent title still returns a success message, as no existence check is performed.
Searching with an empty term returns all books (the LIKE pattern matches everything).
SQL injection strings are interpolated directly into queries, potentially altering behavior.
contract.intent: Expose a web API for basic library management: adding, viewing, searching, updating, and deleting books, plus member login.
invariants: Each request opens a fresh MySQL connection and closes it before responding.
Only the HTTP methods defined for each route are accepted.
Book titles are treated as unique identifiers for duplicate checks.
Responses are plain text or redirects; no JSON payloads are produced.
Database commits occur only after successful write queries.
The server runs continuously as a Flask application.
io_behavior: POST /add_book with title and author redirects to ./add_book if the title already exists, otherwise redirects to ./view_books.
POST /login_member with username and password returns plain text "Login successful" or "Invalid credentials".
POST /update_book_author with title and new_author returns "Author updated successfully".
POST /delete_book with title returns "Book deleted successfully".
GET /search_books?term=... returns a stringified list of books whose title or author contains the term.
GET /view_books returns a stringified list of all books in the database.
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the Books table on successful add_book.
Updates the Author field of a Books row on update_book_author.
Deletes a Books row on delete_book.
Commits each write operation to the MySQL database.
Issues HTTP redirects for add_book outcomes.
Closes the database connection after each request.

rationale: Core routes and side‑effects are implemented, but error handling, response formats, and SQL‑injection behavior diverge from the contract; missing fields are handled gracefully instead of raising errors, and search/view return JSON rather than plain‑text lists, breaking several edge‑case and invariant expectations.
